source.title: Batch Normalization Sampling
source.authors: Zhaodong Chen; Lei Deng; Guo-Qi Li; Jiawei Sun; Xing Hu; Xin Ma; Yuan Xie

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present, including appendices; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests batch-normalization sampling methods and their effects on convergence and accuracy. It does not test whether gradient-based training from random initialization reaches near-zero training classification error, or any other version in the claim.
record.gate_note: Training curves and validation accuracy/error results concern the paper’s proposed normalization-sampling methods. They do not report training classification error, so they are not rows for these versions. The authors’ BN convergence statements in the introduction and related work cite prior studies.
record.test_reason: The study uses BN and compares its proposed sampling variants with standard BN and other normalization methods. It does not compare accuracy gains or learning-rate tolerance with versus without BN. Figure 1(a) compares computational throughput, which cannot establish V6's optimization benefit. Its own results do not test any supplied version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the conclusion: BN sampling can provide roughly 20% overall training acceleration with negligible accuracy loss in suitable configurations, and VDN achieves comparable accuracy to an existing micro-batch normalization approach. Table 3 reports a maximum throughput improvement of 21.7%. These conclusions do not apply uniformly to all sampling configurations.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies sampling strategies for batch-normalization statistics, not the original claim’s training-error behavior or methods.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 1(a) reports 26.7 versus 17.7, 7.7 versus 5.2, and 5.4 versus 3.1 iterations per second without versus with BN. These are computational throughput comparisons, without corresponding accuracy-progress comparisons.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: BN adds computational overhead per training iteration in the tested ImageNet configurations.

fits_no_version.finding: BN sampling variants generally preserve validation accuracy and convergence at suitable sampling ratios while increasing throughput. Table 3 reports 21.7% greater throughput for DenseNet-121 with FS+VDN. Extremely sparse NS and BS fail to converge on ImageNet, and VDN alone causes gradient explosion in DenseNet-121.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Approximating BN statistics can reduce computational cost, with convergence and accuracy depending on sampling strategy, sampling ratio and architecture.

fits_no_version.finding: In the ImageNet ResNet-18 micro-batch experiment, VDN gives 30.88% top-1 validation error versus 30.96% for group normalization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: VDN achieves validation accuracy comparable to group normalization in the tested micro-batch setting.

record.peer_reviewed: Under review as a conference paper at ICLR 2019
record.problems: The reported accuracy results are validation accuracy/error and convergence curves, not training classification error; they do not establish the claim’s training-error outcomes.
record.rows_left_out: No rows: the reported outcomes measure validation accuracy/error, training speed, statistical-estimation error, or convergence curves, rather than the behavior named by any claim version.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error, including random labels, and its dependence on model size, stopping and regularization.
Teacher-student width and the frequency of spurious local minima.
Training-error degradation with depth in matched plain and residual networks, and the specified initialization exceptions.
Effects of initialization on learning speed and trainable depth.
Recovery, sharpness dynamics and divergence relative to learning-rate stability thresholds.
Accuracy gains and learning-rate tolerance with versus without BN; equally fast and stable training using Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The record's T6 assignment should be T4. Its exclusion rationale is too broad: V6 explicitly concerns accuracy progress and does not require training classification error. The decisive gap is the absence of an accuracy-progress or learning-rate-tolerance comparison with versus without BN. The omitted outcomes are already declared in rows_left_out, so they do not require missing entries.

versions.untested_parts: Whether networks reach zero or near-zero training classification error, including on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 with corrupted or random labels; effects of model size, early stopping and regularization on training error.
Whether student width relative to teacher width changes gradient descent’s likelihood of ending in spurious local minima.
Whether plain versus residual networks, depth, special initialization or normalization determine training classification error.
Whether initialization choices change training speed or trainable depth, including orthogonal versus Gaussian weights and 10,000-layer plain convolutional networks.
Whether training recovers from learning rates above stability limits, sharpness hovers at a threshold, or runs diverge below it.
Whether batch normalization speeds accuracy gains or increases learning-rate tolerance, and whether Fixup permits equally fast and stable training without normalization.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
